annotations.title: Building permit leads with contractor license status

description: Answers "What just got permitted, and who's building it?", "New roofing or solar jobs this week?" or "Which permitted contractors have an active license and insurance?". Returns the newest issued building permits (Tacoma, WA today; more Pacific Northwest cities as permission is granted) with address, declared project value, work description, a trade label and the official record link, each matched where possible to the contractor's Washington L&I license (number, status, expiry, insurance expiry; sole proprietors by license number only). Filter with `trades`, `min_valuation_usd`, `since` and `require_contractor_match`. Owner and applicant names are never returned. Keep the `attribution` notice with the data. For bulk or scheduled pulls priced per permit, the same feed is on the Apify Store (vanakenj45/permit-leads-license-status). You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.05 USDC per call (up to 25 permits) via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

cities.description: City ids to include. Default: every city currently available.

max_permits.description: Most permits to return, newest first (1-25). Default 10.

min_match_confidence.description: Lowest match confidence to show a contractor (high = license number; medium = one exact-name active business; low = weaker).

min_valuation_usd.description: Only permits whose declared project value is at least this.

require_contractor_match.description: Only permits matched to a contractor license.

since.description: Start date (inclusive), e.g. 2026-11-01. Default: 30 days ago.

statuses.description: Permit statuses to include: in_review, issued, finaled, expired, cancelled. Default: issued.

trades.description: Only these trades: new_construction, addition_alteration, roofing, solar, hvac_mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire_protection, demolition, sign, site, right_of_way, utility, other. Default: all.

via.description: Optional: the tool whose next_calls suggested this call (filled in for you).
